dcf.method: 5-year FCFF: EBITDA - tax on EBIT - capex - change in net working capital; growth fades linearly from the starting rate to the year-5 rate; Gordon terminal value; equity = EV - borrowings.

blocks.text: Tenneco Clean Air India Ltd (TCAIL) is the Indian listed arm of US-based Tenneco, which is owned by funds advised by Apollo Global Management [F] (AR2026 p.296). It makes two families of products for vehicle makers (OEMs). The first is **Clean Air & Powertrain Solutions (CAPT)**: exhaust after-treatment (catalytic converters, DPF, SCR, mufflers, pipes) plus engine bearings, sealings and Champion spark plugs. The second is **Advanced Ride Technologies (ART)**: Monroe shock absorbers, struts and suspension systems [F] (AR2026 p.13). It earns money by assembling and supplying these parts to OEM programmes for the life of a vehicle platform [F] (CALL Dec 2025). A small share goes to the aftermarket, mainly through the fellow subsidiary Motocare India [F] (AR2026 p.46).

FY26 consolidated revenue was Rs 5,404 cr, EBITDA Rs 925 cr (17% OPM) and PAT Rs 604 cr [F] (NUMBERS). Management prefers value-added revenue (VAR), which strips out ceramic substrates. Substrates are bought at the OEM's direction and passed through at cost [F] (AR2026 p.46). On that basis FY26 VAR was Rs 4,918 cr with an 18.8% EBITDA margin [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). For the TTM to Jun 2026 our data shows sales of Rs 5,663 cr and PAT of Rs 602 cr [F] (NUMBERS).

subsections.title: Bear thesis: reasons not to own it

items: 1. **Valuation sits far above any modelled value.** At Rs 495 the price is 2.2x the bull-case DCF value of Rs 227.3 [E]. The reverse DCF implies 37% sales CAGR for five years against 7.1% in the base case [F] (NUMBERS).

2. **FY26 operating cash flow is not a clean signal.** CFO of Rs 1,429 cr includes a Rs 704.9 cr inflow from 'financial and other assets' [F] (AR2026 p.256). That coincides with collection of the Rs 829.35 cr Motocare sale consideration from a fellow subsidiary [F] (AR2026 p.305). Excluding it, CFO is about Rs 725 cr [E].

3. **Cash went to the parent before the IPO.** Dividends of Rs 1,036.6 cr in FY26 (172% payout) were paid entirely to Tenneco group entities before listing, Rs 885.6 cr of it to the Mauritius parent [F] (AR2026 p.302; NUMBERS). Equity fell from Rs 1,610 cr to Rs 1,198 cr [F] (NUMBERS). That shrinkage is what lifts reported ROCE to 94% [F] (AR2026 p.320).
4. **Customer concentration is rising.** Three customers made up 50.2% of FY26 revenue against 46.3% in FY25 [E] (AR2026 p.313).

5. **Clean Air, the higher-margin franchise, is barely growing.** CAPT VAR grew 5.5% in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.47). Standalone (Clean Air) EBITDA was roughly flat at about Rs 471 cr against Rs 468 cr [E] (AR2026 p.193). The company is absent from the largest PV OEM until around 2028-29 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

6. **Value leakage to the parent is structural.** Royalty of Rs 119.2 cr plus new 'network fees' of Rs 22.8 cr equal 15% of FY26 EBITDA [E] (AR2026 p.300). The group has withdrawn its APA application on royalty pricing [F] (AR2026 p.326).
7. **Margins are under commodity pressure.** Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin on VAR fell 175 bps YoY to 17.9% [F] (PPT Aug 2026). Non-indexed inputs are only partly recovered [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

8. **Capex is stepping up sharply.** FY27 capex is guided at Rs 350-450 cr against Rs 115 cr gross in FY26 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) [F] (AR2026 p.256). That will dilute the asset-turnover story during ramp-up [AI].
9. **There is a promoter supply overhang.** The promoter holds 74.79% [F] (NUMBERS) and has already monetised Rs 3,600 cr through a pure OFS [F] (AR2026 p.58).

10. **Control and compliance lapses.** Books are not backed up daily on Indian servers [F] (AR2026 p.324). The audit trail was not enabled at database level [F] (AR2026 p.327). Export receivables of Rs 16.5 cr are overdue beyond the RBI's nine-month limit [F] (AR2026 p.326).

**Is this an EV-loser or EV-agnostic?** Prior analyst notes frame the risk as powertrain transition [F] (BOARD). But ART, which works on both EVs and combustion vehicles, is now over half of VAR [E] (AR2026 p.47-48). The market may overstate EV risk on the whole company. It may also understate it for Clean Air, which appears to carry the higher margin [AI].

**Order book quality.** Rs 12,400 cr sounds large. It is lifetime value based on OEM volume forecasts, and the AR itself lists 'lack of firm volume commitments' as a risk [F] (AR2026 p.54). Bulls treat it as backlog; bears may be right to treat it as nominations [AI].

**ROCE of 94% vs 61%.** The company's 94% uses tangible net worth after Rs 1,036.6 cr of dividends and excludes the capital reserve [F] (AR2026 p.320). Our data shows 61% [F] (NUMBERS). Underlying returns are high either way. The headline overstates the improvement [AI].

**Cash conversion.** Management says 50-60% of EBITDA converts to cash [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). The reported CFO/PAT of 2.37x is inflated by the Motocare receivable [E] (AR2026 p.256). The truth sits in between and is unproven for a full clean year [AI].
**Margin trajectory.** Bulls point to new technology lifting ART margins [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Bears point to listing costs, commodities and ramp-up of two new plants [AI].

blocks.text: Our variant view is that the market is paying for a growth company built on a short, engineered history [AI]. The listed perimeter was assembled in March 2025 [F] (AR2026 p.260). A Rs 829 cr non-core asset was sold to a fellow subsidiary and the cash went back to the parent as pre-IPO dividends [F] (AR2026 p.260; AR2026 p.302). The reported FY26 cash flow, ROCE and payout therefore describe a recapitalisation, not steady-state economics [AI]. The operating business is good: high share, negative working capital and a real technology edge in ART [F] (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.11). Even so, the bull-case DCF of Rs 227.3 is less than half the price [F] (NUMBERS). For the price to be justified, the order book must convert at a pace no disclosed number yet supports [AI].

The promoter group's 74.79% [F] (NUMBERS) is spread across several Tenneco entities, of which the Mauritius holdco holds 60.22% [F] (AR2026 p.58).

The plants and customer relationships are decades old [F] (AR2026 p.11). The listed entity, however, is about 18 months old in its current form [AI]. Its consolidated history before FY25 is a pooling-of-interests restatement [F] (AR2026 p.321). The FY23-FY24 lines in our statements data use the pre-combination share count (213.4-313.4 m shares) [F] (NUMBERS). They should not be treated as like-for-like with FY25-FY26 [AI]. Three features of the run-up to the IPO stand out [AI]: the Motocare carve-out to a fellow subsidiary, Rs 1,036.6 cr of pre-IPO dividends, and a 100% OFS. Together they show the structure was optimised for the seller.

3. Raw materials are sourced: steel (indexed to OEM pricing), rubber, plastics and gases. Substrates coated with precious metals are bought from Tier-II suppliers at the OEM's direction [F] (AR2026 p.46) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

5. Testing and end-of-line inspection, then delivery to OEM lines on 30-90 day credit [F] (AR2026 p.290).
6. Programme runs for 5-7 years, with annual price-downs and quarterly steel escalators [MC] (CALL Dec 2025; CALL Jun 2026).

blocks.text: Value is captured at nomination: once homologated, the supplier is locked in for the platform's life [AI] (BOARD). Margin then comes from conversion efficiency (P3) and localisation [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Substrates add revenue but no margin [F] (AR2026 p.46). The parent captures a slice up front through royalty and network fees of Rs 142 cr, 2.6% of revenue [E] (AR2026 p.292). Our estimate of the standalone Clean Air business is roughly 26% EBITDA on VAR, against about 18.8% consolidated [E] (AR2026 p.193). That implies ART and the powertrain subsidiaries earn lower margins than Clean Air. This is inferred from entity accounts; segment margins are not disclosed [AI].

Capex ran at 1.3-1.8% of sales in FY23-FY26 [F] (NUMBERS). Fixed-asset turnover is 9.29x [F] (NUMBERS). Management cites Rs 3.5-4 of steady-state revenue per rupee of gross capex [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). Some capex is equipment transferred from other Tenneco regions [MC] (CALL Dec 2025). That flatters asset turnover and is a form of group support not priced in the accounts we can see [AI]. The model is **asset-light** today. FY27 guidance of Rs 350-450 cr is 6.5-8.3% of FY26 revenue [E] and temporarily moves it toward moderate intensity.

items: CAPT per management [MC] (AR2026 p.46; CALL Aug 2026): absence from the leading Japanese PV OEM (about 50% of the small-car segment, which benefited from the GST cut), intra- and inter-OEM mix shifts, EU-origin vehicle imports, and EV substitution at a European OEM. Like-for-like market growth after removing EVs and that OEM is said to be 8-10%, against CAPT's 9.6% in Q1 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

CAPT, our read [AI]: management's growth explanation keeps shifting. It was CV pull-ahead in Q2 [MC] (CALL Dec 2025), GST small cars in Q3 [MC] (CALL Feb 2026), and EV plus Japanese OEM mix in Q1 FY27 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). The consistent fact is that CAPT has trailed its served market for four quarters [F] (CALL Aug 2026). Substrate revenue fell 4.8% [F] (AR2026 p.47), consistent with lower precious-metal loading or mix [AI].
ART per management [MC] (CALL Aug 2026): volumes, GST-driven small-car demand, new programmes, DCx adoption and four new customers.

ART, our read [AI]: growth outpaced PV production (+9.5% in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.40)) by about 10 points, so share gain and content are real. But utilisation above 90% [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) means near-term growth is capacity-constrained until the West India plant opens.

blocks.text: Both segments are programme-driven [AI]. Revenue follows OEM production schedules on nominated platforms, with no firm volume commitments [F] (AR2026 p.54). ART's FY26 step-up is more exposed to a few new programmes (DCx flagship) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). CAPT is more exposed to emission-norm timing (TREM V, CAFE 3, BS-VII) [MC] (CALL Dec 2025). Neither is tender-based [AI].

subsections.title: Case studies, contracts and the verdict on concentration

items: Case studies: the DCx flagship SUV programme is developed with a leading Indian OEM [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). A modular in-line BS6 system was built for a global CV OEM, ~Rs 115 cr/yr potential [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). A Euro 7 proof of concept was completed with a European truck OEM [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

Contract form: business is won as programme nominations, with no firm long-term volume commitments [F] (AR2026 p.54). Steel has quarterly escalators [MC] (CALL Jun 2026); other inputs are negotiated case by case [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). No long-term agreements are disclosed [F].

Verdict [AI]: concentration is worsening on the only disclosed measure (top-3 at 50.2%). Management's counter is that four new ART customers were added in Q1 FY27 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026) and that Japanese OEM panel entries are coming [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Neither yet shows in revenue.

blocks.text: The client base is high quality and sticky by design [AI]. Every named growth client is either already large (the Indian SUV OEM, CV OEMs) or still years from revenue (the Japanese PV OEM, exports) [AI]. Intra-group channels (Motocare plus Tenneco exports) are about 6% of revenue [E] (AR2026 p.298-299). They are priced within the group, which minorities cannot test [AI].

The company discloses a half-yearly 'incremental lifetime order book'. It is defined as 'all orders secured based on OEM confirmation on volume and price, but not put into production', with visibility over about 5-6 years [F] (AR2026 p.8). The book stood at Rs 9,840 cr on 30 Sep 2025, including Rs 1,760 cr of exports [MC] (CALL Dec 2025), and at Rs 12,400 cr on 31 Mar 2026 [F] (AR2026 p.49). Management declined a Q1 update: 'there's no steady order book... we decided that we would report order book every half-year' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). It claims the book gives '100% visibility of our FY 2028 internal revenue target' [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). **The target itself is not disclosed** [F].

blocks.text: The CRISIL clean-air market excludes substrates, which TCAIL books as revenue [F] (AR2026 p.45). Comparing the two directly is invalid [AI]. A better frame is to build from disclosed parts [AI]. Start with ART revenue of Rs 2,488.5 cr growing with PV production (+9.5% in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.40)) plus share and content gains. items: Discount rate: the model lists a 0.3 debt weight and a 7.5% post-tax cost of debt, yet the WACC equals the 15.0% cost of equity [F] (NUMBERS). In effect it discounts at cost of equity, which suits a company with no bank debt [AI]. The 7% ERP and 1.15 beta are conservative for a net-cash subsidiary earning a 43% ROE [AI].
Growth: the 4.3% starting rate is anchored to a 3-year CAGR (3.8%) built on non-comparable FY23-FY24 data [F] (NUMBERS) [AI]. It is low against FY26 VAR growth of 12.3% [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

Net cash is not added to equity value [F] (NUMBERS). Royalty and network fees are embedded in the 17% margin [AI].
Net read: the model is conservative on growth and discount rate and generous on capex. None of these adjustments, within the model's own sensitivity range, closes a gap of more than 2x [AI].

blocks.text: At the base margin, WACC and terminal growth, today's EV requires **about 37% a year sales growth for five years**, against a base-case 5-year equivalent of 7.1% [F] (NUMBERS). For comparison: our data's 3-year sales CAGR is 3.8% [F] (NUMBERS); FY26 revenue growth was 10.5% and VAR growth 12.3% [E] [MC] (CALL Jun 2026); Q1 FY27 revenue growth was 20.1% [F] (NUMBERS); the bull case runs at 8.8-13% [F] (NUMBERS). Compounding 37% for five years multiplies sales about 4.8x, to roughly Rs 27,200 cr from Rs 5,663 cr [E]. That is more than twice the entire Rs 12,400 cr lifetime order book [F] (AR2026 p.49).

The price embeds an outcome that neither the order book, the capacity plan nor management's own 'double-digit' language supports [AI]. Guided FY27 capex of Rs 350-450 cr implies Rs 1,050-1,800 cr of steady-state revenue on management's 1:3-1:4 rule [E] (CALL Feb 2026). The reverse DCF requires about Rs 21,600 cr of additional sales [E]. The market is either applying a far lower discount rate than 15%, or capitalising a scarcity/quality premium for a high-ROCE MNC auto ancillary [AI].

Indian auto-component MNC subsidiaries often trade on multiples, not 15%-WACC DCFs [AI]. A business with 43% ROE, negative working capital, net cash and 18% recent VAR growth may deserve a much lower discount rate and a longer high-growth runway than five years [AI]. In that framing, P/E 33x and EV/EBITDA 21x [F] (NUMBERS) are the relevant metrics, and the DCF gap mostly reflects model conservatism [AI]. We note the argument but cannot test it against peer multiples, which are not in our evidence set [F].

blocks.text: A market leader with 55-68% shares [MC] (AR2026 p.11), 61% ROCE, net cash [F] (NUMBERS) and a visible structural growth engine in ART (+27.9% in Q1 FY27) [F] (CALL Aug 2026). The listed entity's reported FY26 economics are shaped by a pre-IPO recapitalisation: a related-party asset sale collected through CFO, a 172% payout to the parent and an OFS exit [F] (AR2026 p.256; p.302; p.58). Clean Air growth is weak [F] (AR2026 p.47). Concentration is rising [E] (AR2026 p.313), and recurring parent charges take a quarter of PAT [E]. subsections.title: What the market may be missing

items: Upside it may miss [AI]: our DCF's starting growth (4.3%) sits well below current run-rates. ART may be in an early adoption curve that a five-year fade model cannot capture.

Downside it may miss [AI]: Clean Air, which appears to be the higher-margin half, is flat at EBITDA level. Consolidated margin is therefore drifting toward ART's lower level, while the market extrapolates FY26 cash flow and ROCE that were flattered by the recapitalisation.

blocks.text: Five-year possibility space [E]: year-5 sales range from Rs 6,678 cr (bear) to Rs 9,496 cr (bull) in our model [F] (NUMBERS). The price implies roughly Rs 27,200 cr [E] (reverse DCF arithmetic). The realistic space disclosed by the company (order book, capacity plan, regulation) sits inside the model range, not near the implied figure [AI].

blocks.text: At Rs 495 the stock trades 4.6x the bear value, 2.9x the base value and 2.2x the bull value [E] (NUMBERS). It is 25% above the Rs 397 IPO price and 25% below its 52-week high [E] (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.210). The gap reflects three things: the market's lower implied discount rate and longer growth runway, a scarcity premium for a high-ROCE MNC ancillary, and extrapolation of FY26 cash flow and returns that our forensic work shows were flattered [AI]. This is not a rating and carries no price target.

summary.one_line: Tenneco Clean Air India is a high-share, net-cash auto-component franchise with a real growth engine in suspension (ART), but its reported FY26 cash flow, ROCE and payout were shaped by a pre-IPO recapitalisation for the parent, and at Rs 495 the shares trade at 2.2x even the bull-case DCF value (Rs 227.3), implying about 37% annual sales growth that no disclosed order book, capacity plan or guidance supports.
bull_points: ART is a structural share-gainer: VAR +19.7% in FY26 and +27.9% in Q1 FY27, PV shock-absorber share up to 55%, DCx flagship programme worth ~Rs 220 cr a year [F] (AR2026 p.48; CALL Aug 2026) [MC] (PPT Aug 2026; CALL Feb 2026).

Lifetime order book rose from Rs 9,840 cr to Rs 12,400 cr in six months after Rs 3,465 cr moved to production; management says it covers 100% of its FY28 internal target [F] (AR2026 p.49) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).
Market leadership (58% CV and 68% off-highway clean air) with homologation switching costs and regulation-driven content growth from CAFE 3 and BS-VII [MC] (AR2026 p.11; CALL Jun 2026).
Capital-light and net cash: ROCE 61%, fixed-asset turnover 9.29x, CCC -33 days, Rs 571 cr cash and capex funded internally [F] (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.254) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).
bear_points: Price is 2.2x the bull DCF value (Rs 227.3) and 2.9x the base (Rs 172.6); the reverse DCF requires ~37% sales CAGR for five years against 7.1% in the base case [F] (NUMBERS).
FY26 CFO of Rs 1,429 cr includes ~Rs 705 cr from collecting the Rs 829 cr Motocare sale receivable from a fellow subsidiary. Excluding it, CFO is ~Rs 725 cr [F] (AR2026 p.256; p.305) [E].
Rs 1,036.6 cr of pre-IPO dividends (172% payout) went entirely to group entities before a 100% OFS; the shrunken equity drives the 94% headline ROCE [F] (AR2026 p.302; p.58; p.320).

Top-3 customer share rose to 50.2% from 46.3%; recurring parent royalty plus network fees (Rs 142 cr) take ~23.5% of PAT, and the royalty APA was withdrawn [E] (AR2026 p.313; p.300) [F] (AR2026 p.326).

Clean Air is barely growing: CAPT VAR +5.5% in FY26 and standalone EBITDA roughly flat. Q1 FY27 VAR EBITDA margin fell 175 bps on non-indexed commodity costs [F] (AR2026 p.47; PPT Aug 2026) [E] (AR2026 p.193).
